| f-006 | defect | MAJOR | The new session-level advisory lock unlocks ordinary closure returns, including `Result::Err`, but it is not safe under panic or future cancellation. Both bypass the explicit `pg_advisory_unlock`. SQLx 0.8.6 returns `PoolConnection` to the pool on Drop unless `close_on_drop` was set, so the PostgreSQL session — and its advisory lock — survive. Reacquiring that same session is re-entrant and one later unlock leaves the leaked hold behind; another session blocks. The helper also consumes one of a fixed eight pool connections while its closure acquires separate connections from the same pool. `worker_concurrency` has no upper bound, so eight distinct ingest jobs can each hold a lock connection and then all wait forever for a ninth connection. No test calls `with_conversation_lock`. Smallest boring fix: use a globally serial ingest lane first, or make the lock guard close its connection on every abnormal drop and bound lock holders below pool capacity; then prove same-key mutual exclusion, different-key progress, closure error, panic/cancellation recovery, and configured high worker concurrency. | /Users/jordanknight/substrate/flowspace/fs3-convo-ingest/crates/store/src/ingest_cursors.rs:426-485; /Users/jordanknight/substrate/flowspace/fs3-convo-ingest/crates/store/src/lib.rs:183-214; /Users/jordanknight/substrate/flowspace/fs3-convo-ingest/crates/core/src/config.rs:850-899; /Users/jordanknight/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/sqlx-core-0.8.6/src/pool/connection.rs:18-25,91-99,198-210 | — | Round 3 detached connection and try-lock fix the panic/cancellation and pool-slot mechanisms. | f-009 | defect | MAJOR | Lock contention now completes the losing ingest job successfully without reading the file. The comment's premise that the winner is reading the same bytes is false for a live-growing session: the winner can read through offset N, new bytes can arrive while it still holds the lock, and a later explicit ingest can fail `pg_try_advisory_lock`, return `Ok(None)`, and be marked done. The winner commits N; the later job that could have read N+delta has disappeared, and no future poll is guaranteed for this pull-based feature. This narrows F-006 by replacing deadlock with silent deferral/loss of the request. Smallest fix: represent contention as retry/park, or deterministically enqueue one canonical follow-up after the holder releases; do not settle the job as success. Add a test that appends after the holder's read while a second route contends, then proves the later bytes land without a third invocation. | /Users/jordanknight/substrate/flowspace/fs3-convo-ingest/crates/store/src/ingest_cursors.rs:439-492; /Users/jordanknight/substrate/flowspace/fs3-convo-ingest/crates/daemon/src/convo_ingest.rs:452-465,601-610; /Users/jordanknight/substrate/flowspace/fs3-convo-ingest/crates/daemon/src/convo_ingest.rs:188-195 | — | — | — | — | [ac-0003](../../plan.dd.md#acceptance-criteria) | Source trace: try-lock false returns Ok(None); ingest converts that to continue and ultimately Ok(report); run discards the report and returns Ok, so the queue settles the contending job done.
